title: Life Cycle of Plasmodium & Malarial Pathogenesis
topic: Dual-Host Schizogony, Hemozoin Toxin, & Anopheles Vector Transmission
quickSummary: Plasmodium dual-host cycle: Human (intermediate host: asexual schizogony in liver cells, then erythrocytic schizogony in RBCs releasing Hemozoin toxin that causes recurring chills and high fever). Mosquito (definitive host: sexual syngamy in midgut, motile ookinete, oocyst sporogony, sporozoites stored in salivary glands).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Life Cycle of Plasmodium: Dual-Host Mechanics
conceptBreakdown.title: Life Cycle of Plasmodium: Dual-Host Mechanics

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Plasmodium completes a digenetic life cycle: (1) Human Host: asexual schizogony in hepatocytes followed by erythrocyte invasion and lysis with Hemozoin release (causing fever and chills); (2) Female Anopheles: sexual syngamy in stomach midgut, ookinete, oocyst, and sporogony releasing sporozoites into salivary glands.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 2.1 Asexual Cycle in Human Host (Intermediate Host)
1. **Inoculation**: Female *Anopheles* mosquito injects motile, spindle-shaped **Sporozoites** into human blood with its saliva during a blood meal.
2. **Exo-Erythrocytic (Hepatic) Schizogony**: Sporozoites enter liver cells (hepatocytes) within 30 minutes, reproducing asexually to generate thousands of **Merozoites**, which burst hepatocytes.
3. **Erythrocytic Schizogony**: Merozoites invade Red Blood Cells (RBCs) $\rightarrow$ Trophozoite (Signet Ring stage) $\rightarrow$ Amoeboid stage $\rightarrow$ Schizont.
4. **Hemozoin Release**: Digestion of hemoglobin by trophozoites converts toxic free heme into insoluble crystalline **Hemozoin**. Synchronous bursting of RBCs releases merozoites and Hemozoin into blood, triggering cyclic high fever spikes and shaking chills every $48\text{--}72\text{ hours}$.
5. **Gametocytogenesis**: A fraction of merozoites differentiate inside RBCs into male (microgametocytes) and female (macrogametocytes) **Gametocytes**.

### 2.2 Sexual Cycle in Mosquito Host (Definitive Host)
1. **Ingestion**: Female *Anopheles* mosquito sucks human blood containing mature gametocytes.
2. **Syngamy (Fertilization)**: In the mosquito midgut lumen, microgametes fertilize macrogametes to form a diploid zygote that matures into a motile **Ookinete**.
3. **Oocyst & Sporogony**: Ookinete penetrates the peritrophic membrane and gut wall, encysting on the outer stomach wall as an **Oocyst**. The oocyst undergoes asexual sporogony, generating thousands of **Sporozoites**.
4. **Salivary Gland Migration**: Mature oocyst ruptures, releasing sporozoites into hemolymph, which migrate to and lodge in the **Salivary Glands**, ready for inoculation into the next host.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Plasmodium Species Differentiation
conceptBreakdown.title: Plasmodium Species Differentiation
conceptBreakdown.content: Plasmodium falciparum causes malignant, severe tertian malaria with high mortality due to cytoadherence in cerebral capillaries; P. vivax and P. ovale cause benign tertian malaria (48h cycle); P. malariae causes quartan malaria (72h cycle).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Sir Ronald Ross Discovery
conceptBreakdown.title: Sir Ronald Ross Discovery
conceptBreakdown.content: Sir Ronald Ross (1897, Secunderabad, India) discovered the transmission of malaria by female Anopheles mosquitoes by identifying oocysts on the mosquito stomach wall, winning the 1902 Nobel Prize in Medicine.
